newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan doomsday guru again ejected from Tokyo court.
newsitem.headline: Japan doomsday guru again ejected from Tokyo court.

text.p: Japanese doomsday cult leader Shoko Asahara was thrown out of court again on Thursday for disrupting his murder trial.
It was the fourth time he has been ejected from his trial for the Tokyo subway gassing and other murders.

The 41-year-old Asahara, founder of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), was told to leave the Tokyo District Court within 20 minutes of the start of proceedings on the 1989 killing of an anti-cult lawyer, his wife and their baby.

The bearded, nearly blind guru taunted the three-judge panel and thrashed in his seat during testimony by ex-follower Kazuaki Okazaki, one of six cultists accused of killing lawyer Tsutsumi Sakamoto and his family in November 1989.
"Why don"t you send me out of the court, judge? Am I being kidnapped or something?" Asahara said.
"The testimony is a lie," Asahara shouted when Okazaki, 36, testified that Asahara ordered the murder of Sakamoto, who was helping families get their children out of the cult.
"I never said to kill him," Asahara said.

Asahara and five others, including Okazaki, have been indicted on charges of killing the family, whose disappearance went unsolved for six years until investigations into the March 1995 sarin nerve gas attack on the Tokyo subway system.
Okazaki and three others have pleaded guilty to the murder charges.
Asahara has refused to enter pleas on any of 17 major charges he faces. They include murder and weapon and drug manufacturing charges.
Witnesses in early proceedings testified that Asahara ordered the subway gassing, which killed 12 and made thousands ill.
The witnesses have said the guru believed the attack would set off chaos which would bring down Japan"s government, allowing Asahara to take control of the country.
